statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail 17 sits in the low band and well below the block threshold, while Stress 47 is elevated and Confidence 87 is high.
recommendation: The deterministic mapping from Tail 17 produces EA_ON with a green status, pause false and caution false. headline: NQ posts a fifth consecutive higher overnight extreme at 29,288 and holds near it, now with European cash confirming for the first time; VIX 14.89, flat yields and lower oil keep Tail at 17 and Stress at 47
body:
The observation that moves this hour is that the overnight extension sequence has both lengthened and gained its first cross-market confirmation. Yahoo Finance shows NQ at 29,277.00, up 171.25 points or 0.59% on the 29,105.75 settle, with the overnight band at 29,017.00-29,288.25; Investing.com shows 29,243.50, up 137.75 points or 0.47%, on a delayed stamp. The 29,288.25 high is the fifth successive higher extreme after 29,168.25, 29,197.00, 29,225.00 and 29,266.00 in the preceding four hours, and price is holding within roughly eleven points of it. Repeated extension combined with holding near the extreme is the structure this measure treats as evidence that retracements are becoming shallow, so Tail is carried from 15 to 17.

What is genuinely new is the European cash open. Through the Asian session the advance was a divergence: Business Standard reported Nasdaq futures down 0.08% at 03:34Z while MSCI Asia ex-Japan fell 0.5%, the Nikkei 0.9% and the Kospi 2.7%. European cash has now opened higher instead, with the Stoxx 600 up about 0.4%, the DAX 0.29%, the FTSE 100 0.21% and Euro Stoxx 50 futures 0.34%. A futures bid that regional cash equities decline to follow is a divergence; one they do follow is confirmation, and that is why this hour is scored above the last rather than equal to it.

What prevents a larger reading is amplitude and the character of the move. A 271-point overnight range is 0.93%, unremarkable, and each leg higher has taken roughly an hour rather than arriving as an impulse. The advance remains a partial repair of Monday's chip-led decline rather than a breakout. The cross-asset set is calm to de-escalating: VIX closed at 14.89, down 6.0% from 15.84 with a 14.77 low; the 2-year is 4.25% and the 10-year 4.70%, both effectively unchanged; and oil is falling rather than gapping, with WTI at $84.50, down 0.60%, and Brent at $91.52, down 0.70%, after the expanded US sanctions campaign aimed at Iran, with shipments continuing through the Strait of Hormuz. That is the opposite of an aligned amplifier stack.

The identified catalysts are concentrated rather than systemic. Monday's semiconductor decline followed reports that Nvidia notified customers AI server prices will rise more than 15% on soaring memory costs, and the separate 50% Canadian auto and steel tariff threat announced for January 2027 transmitted to automakers and steel rather than to index-level technology. Shared Finviz cross-asset context, collected at 06:20Z and used only as delayed supporting evidence, is consistent with the live picture: NQ futures +0.49%, ES +0.15%, VIX futures -0.22%, Treasury futures flat and crude -0.85%, against a latest-session semiconductor complex in which all seven tracked names fell for a mean of -3.03% and a megacap set that was mixed with 2.06% dispersion. Delayed context of that kind is treated as confirmation of tone, never as live price-path evidence.

The conditional path stays inside the low Tail band for all 24 hours, so every slot maps to EA_ON. It opens at 17 on the observed fifth overnight high, eases through the European morning to a floor of 13 in the calendar-empty hours, rebuilds to 15 at 12:00Z for the Fed Barkin and weekly ADP checkpoints, reaches 18 at 13:00Z as Case-Shiller prints and the 13:30Z cash open follows, and peaks at 19 at 14:00Z where CB Consumer Confidence, New Home Sales and the Richmond Fed index all land thirty minutes into cash trade. That peak stays below the block threshold because every US release today is medium impact and no post-release price path can be observed in advance. The horizon then decays through the US afternoon, falls to 11 overnight, and drifts back to 16 by the final slot as Wednesday's high-impact 12:30Z cluster and Nvidia's after-close results come into view, with options pricing about a 5.4% post-earnings move against a 7.4% twelve-quarter average.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry a published Claude assessment. The window opened at 07:00Z on 24 August with its structural peak already in place: the European cash open produced Tail 19 with Stress 58 in a trend-down mode, which faded to 17 within an hour and to 12 by 09:00Z, then held an 11 to 13 band through the European morning. The only non-green slots surrounded the US cash open: Tail 20 with Stress 54 in an event/whipsaw mode at 13:00Z, mapping to WATCH, and the single peak at 14:00Z, which reached Tail 26 with Stress 60 in a trend-down mode and mapped to BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES. That peak decayed immediately, to 13 by 15:00Z and into single digits from 17:00Z as the US afternoon mean-reverted, running a 7 to 10 Tail band with Stress easing from 46 to 42. The overnight hours held a 9 to 13 band with Stress near 45 to 47, and the final three slots carried Tail 13, 14 and 15 in a trend-up mode as the overnight extension sequence developed. Sixteen of the 24 slots carried a mixed mode.
outlookSummary: The conditional path stays inside the low Tail band for all 24 hours, so every slot maps to EA_ON. It opens at 17 on the observed fifth consecutive higher overnight extreme and the first European cash confirmation of the advance, then steps down through the European morning, 16 and 15, to 14 and a floor of 13 in the calendar-empty hours before the US day. The series rebuilds to 15 at 12:00Z for the Fed Barkin and weekly ADP checkpoints, reaches 18 at 13:00Z as Case-Shiller prints and the cash open follows at 13:30Z, and peaks at 19 at 14:00Z for the CB Consumer Confidence, New Home Sales and Richmond Fed cluster. That is the highest conditional reading of the horizon and it remains below the block threshold, because today's US calendar carries no high-impact release and no post-event price path can be observed in advance. It decays to 17 and then 15 through the US morning, holds 14 across the afternoon and the 17:00Z two-year auction, steps to 15 for the power hour and the 20:00Z close, and falls to 12 and then 11 after the cash session ends. The overnight stretch runs 11 to 13 before drifting to 14, 15 and 16 in the final three slots as Wednesday's Core PCE, second GDP estimate and durable goods cluster, and Nvidia's results after that day's close, come into view. Stress traces the same shape one band higher, from 44 to 47 overnight to a 56 peak at 14:00Z and back to 52 at the horizon's end, while Confidence decays from 87 to 64 with distance from observed evidence. The narrow danger window is 13:30Z to 14:30Z, spanning the cash open and the medium-impact release cluster.
